items.title: Separately adopted fixed-background Maxwell and charged probes
items.physical_scope: A separately adopted classical test model on a prescribed smooth Lorentzian metric: smooth source-free or prescribed-source Maxwell fields and massive charged probes on finite local-potential worldline segments. The metric and field are fixed inputs; no Einstein equation is imposed on them, no probe self-field or self-gravity is evaluated, and no small-backreaction limit, global potential, global trajectory, or empirical validity is asserted. Geometric-optics use is limited to the exact finite-order phase, amplitude, constraint, and compact-region bounds in the listed mathematical supplier.

items.statement:
On an open region of the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime and length-coordinate SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]], adopt a prescribed-background Maxwell model. The metric $g$ is fixed input. Choose a real $C^2$ electromagnetic two-form $F$ and either adopt the source-free equations $dF=0$ and $d(\star_gF)=0$, or supply a $C^1$ current $j$ and adopt $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, with the exact signs and units of that definition. The source current is prescribed independently of the probe; this postulate does not impose an Einstein equation, matter evolution equation, or field equation for the sources on the unchanged metric.

For a massive charged probe, use the adopted local action and finite-curve conditions of [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]]: $m>0$ and $q$ are constant, the path is a $C^2$ future-directed timelike segment parameterized by proper time, and its endpoints are fixed in variations supported in a local potential domain $V$ with a supplied $C^2$ one-form $A$ satisfying $dA=F$. The potential and metric are external data independent of the path. Under the exact hypotheses of [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]], action stationarity is equivalent to $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$; that theorem's $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption is inherited only when this equivalent force-law formulation is used. No global potential or trajectory is included.

The probe's own singular field and self-gravity are excluded. No radiation reaction, variable mass or charge, finite-body model, or backreaction estimate is adopted. In particular, calling $g$ or $F$ a test background records this model's omission of their response; it does not claim that the unchanged pair solves the coupled Einstein–Maxwell equations or is close to a coupled solution.

When geometric optics is invoked, it is restricted to the exact $C^4$ real phase, $C^3$ complex amplitudes, four pointwise ansatz constraints, and fixed compact-chart coefficient bounds of [[lem-emg-controlled-maxwell-wkb]]. That result supplies finite residual and leading-field estimates, local null rays, and a polarization quotient; it supplies no convergent series, global transport through caustics, exact-solution error estimate, or backreaction theorem.

This is a separately adopted physical model with no empirical premise. The Maxwell and probe assumptions are not deductions from one another, from mathematical axioms, or from source authority.

items.statement:
Use the fixed-background Maxwell test model of [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]] on a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and its adopted length-coordinate SI conventions. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Let $\theta\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ be dimensionless, set $k=d\theta$, and assume $k$ is nowhere zero and $g^{-1}(k,k)=0$. Let $a_0,a_1\in C^3(U;T^*M\otimes_\mathbb R\mathbb C)$, with covariant derivatives and contractions extended complex-linearly. Use $[k]=\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, $[a_0]=[a_1]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, and dimensionless $\epsilon$, as in [[lem-emg-controlled-maxwell-wkb]]. Define

$$ (\Box a)_b:=g^{ac}\nabla_a\nabla_c a_b,\qquad (Pa)_b:=(\Box a)_b-\operatorname{Ric}_b{}^c a_c,\qquad (La)_b:=2k^c\nabla_ca_b+(\nabla_ck^c)a_b. $$

Assume the four pointwise constraints $g^{-1}(k,a_0)=0$, $La_0=0$, $iLa_1+Pa_0=0$, and $ik^a(a_1)_a+\nabla^a(a_0)_a=0$. For $0<\epsilon\le1$, form the complex ansatz $A_\epsilon=\epsilon e^{i\theta/\epsilon}(a_0+\epsilon a_1)$ and its real potential $\widehat A_\epsilon:=\operatorname{Re}A_\epsilon$ with real field $\widehat F_\epsilon:=d\widehat A_\epsilon$. Use the fixed-chart component max norm $\|\cdot\|_{\infty,K}$ of [[lem-emg-controlled-maxwell-wkb]], which is zero on an empty compact set. On a nonempty compact coordinate set $K$, assume finite constants $K_0,D_0,C_0,B_0,B_1$ satisfy $\|k\|_{\infty,K}\le K_0$, $\|d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le D_0$, $\|Pa_1-\nabla d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le C_0$, $\|da_0+ik\wedge a_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_0$, and $\|da_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_1$. The real field obeys $d\widehat F_\epsilon=0$ and

$$ \|\nabla^a(\widehat F_\epsilon)_{ab}\|_{\infty,K}\le\epsilon K_0D_0+\epsilon^2C_0,\qquad \|\widehat F_\epsilon-\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\theta/\epsilon}ik\wedge a_0)\|_{\infty,K}\le\epsilon B_0+\epsilon^2B_1. $$

Each local integral curve of $k^\sharp$ is an affinely parameterized null geodesic. Along it $a_0$ is transported according to the supplied scalar transport amplitude, and the leading physical polarization is the class in $k^\perp/\operatorname{span}_\mathbb C\{k\}$, a two-dimensional complex space with positive induced Hermitian form. These are exact finite-order deductions under the displayed ansatz constraints. The residual is a component norm in the chosen chart, not an observer-independent tensor norm. The conclusion asserts no convergent WKB series, existence of amplitudes across caustics, exact Maxwell solution for a nonzero residual, solution-distance estimate, or coupled Einstein–Maxwell family.

items.statement:
Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, Levi–Civita connection $\nabla$, and length-coordinate SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]] and the separately prescribed Maxwell test model of [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]]. Here $U$ is open, $g$ is the fixed metric, a field strength $F$ is a smooth real two-form, and a prescribed current $j$ is a smooth real vector field. The formal stress tensor and constants are

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}(g,F)=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd},\qquad \kappa=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}>0.$$

The adopted Maxwell alternatives are $dF=0$, $d(\star_gF)=0$ when source-free, or $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ for a separately prescribed current. Let $g$ satisfy $G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=0$ on $U$, where $\Lambda$ is constant. Define the electromagnetic stress residual relative to this unchanged vacuum metric, with no matter stress included, by

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F;\Lambda):=G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F).$$

First let $F_0$ be a smooth source-free Maxwell two-form on $U$. For real dimensionless $\delta$, $F_\delta:=\delta F_0$ remains source-free and

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)=-\kappa\delta^2T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F_0).$$

The same conclusion holds for an actual smooth sourced Maxwell pair: let $F_0$ be a smooth real two-form and $j_0$ a smooth real vector field on $U$ satisfying $dF_0=0$ and $\nabla_a(F_0)^{ab}=-\mu_0j_0^b$. With $F_\delta:=\delta F_0$ and $j_\delta:=\delta j_0$, the pair still satisfies the same sourced Maxwell equations, and

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)=-\kappa\delta^2T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F_0).$$

For a compact set $K$ in a fixed smooth coordinate chart contained in $U$ and a smooth covariant two-tensor $S$, define $\|S\|_{\infty,K}:=\max_{0\le a,b\le3}\sup_{p\in K}|S_{ab}(p)|$ when $K\ne\varnothing$, and set $\|S\|_{\infty,\varnothing}:=0$. In either Maxwell case,

$$\|\mathscr R(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)\|_{\infty,K}=\kappa\delta^2\|T^{\mathrm{EM}}(g,F_0)\|_{\infty,K}.$$

If $\delta\ne0$ and $F_0$ is nonzero at a point, its observer energy is positive there, so this electromagnetic/vacuum-background residual is nonzero. In the sourced case this does not test a full Einstein–Maxwell–matter equation, because no source-matter stress is included in $\mathscr R$. The residual is a consistency calculation, not an estimate of distance to a different metric solution.

Separately, on an open region where smooth charged-dust quantities have $\rho>0$, $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$, $j^a=\sigma U^a$, and the formal matter-exchange equation holds, replacing $(\rho,\sigma)$ by $(\eta\rho,\eta\sigma)$ for $\eta>0$ scales matter stress and current linearly, leaves $\sigma/\rho$ unchanged, and preserves the dust force equation when the prescribed $F,U$ are held fixed. Maxwell's sourced equation must still match the scaled current. If instead both $F$ and $j$ are scaled by $\eta$, the sourced Maxwell system is linear but electromagnetic stress scales as $\eta^2$ while dust stress scales as $\eta$; these degree differences provide no general coupled-solution family.

Finally, for a fixed $Q\ne0$ and $\ell>0$, prescribe only on the finite Minkowski annulus $\mathcal A_\ell=\{\mathbf x:\ell<|\mathbf x|<2\ell\}$ the radial electric field $\mathbf E=Q(4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2)^{-1}\mathbf e_r$, $\mathbf B=0$. Its field energy on that annulus is $Q^2/(16\pi\varepsilon_0\ell)$ and diverges as $\ell\downarrow0$. This calculation defines no field or source at the origin and supplies no point-charge construction or regularization theorem.

items.title: Finite-time weak/slow charged probe correspondence
items.physical_scope: Finite-time comparison for a massive charged test probe on a stationary weak metric with the exact C2 remainder bounds and prescribed electric/magnetic scalings of the mathematical supplier, with a smooth closed background two-form and the adopted action on short local-potential curve segments. It requires alpha nonzero, a sufficiently small parameter cutoff fixed by the uniform bounds, uniformly small speed, existing trajectories, common compact convex state containment in K x R3 and finite scaled duration. It imposes neither the inhomogeneous Maxwell equation nor Einstein equations and constructs no fully coupled background family.

items.statement:
Use the charged-probe action sector of the fixed-background model of [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]] and let $\alpha=q/m\ne0$, with constant $m>0$, constant charge $q$, length scale $L>0$, and speed constant $c>0$. When the Lorentz-force form is obtained from the adopted action, the inherited $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis of that exact action-equivalence theorem is assumed; no stronger choice axiom is used. In SI, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[L]=\mathrm m$, and $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; $\epsilon$, $X$, $\phi$, $\mathbf e$, and $\mathbf b$ are dimensionless. Choose a cutoff $0<\epsilon_*\le1$ sufficiently small in terms of the displayed uniform bounds below, as required by [[thm-emg-weak-slow-test-lorentz-limit]], and fix $0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_*$. On an open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, let $\mathcal K\Subset\Omega$ be compact and convex, use length coordinates $x^0=ct$, $x^i=LX^i$, and suppose the prescribed metric is smooth, stationary and Lorentzian on a neighborhood of $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times L\mathcal K$, with $\partial_0$ future timelike. For a smooth dimensionless $\phi$ and some fixed finite $C_g$, assume for every spatial multi-index $\beta$ with $|\beta|\le2$ that

$$|\partial_X^\beta r_{00}^{(\epsilon)}|+\max_{i,j}|\partial_X^\beta r_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}|\le C_g\epsilon^2,\qquad \max_i|\partial_X^\beta r_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}|\le C_g\epsilon^{3/2},$$

where $g_{00}^{(\epsilon)}=-(1+2\epsilon\phi)+r_{00}^{(\epsilon)}$, $g_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}=(1-2\epsilon\phi)\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}$, and $g_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}=r_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}$. Prescribe smooth stationary dimensionless fields $\mathbf e,\mathbf b$ with values and first derivatives bounded on $\mathcal K$, and a smooth real closed two-form $F^{(\epsilon)}$ on the same background neighborhood, with $dF^{(\epsilon)}=0$ and SI components $F_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}=-E_i^{(\epsilon)}/c$, $F_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k^{(\epsilon)}$ and

$$\alpha\mathbf E^{(\epsilon)}=\frac{\epsilon c^2}{L}\mathbf e,\qquad \alpha\mathbf B^{(\epsilon)}=\frac{\sqrt\epsilon c}{L}\mathbf b.$$

Closure $dF^{(\epsilon)}=0$ ensures local potentials, not a global potential: in each sufficiently small open coordinate ball $D$ about a curve point, use the smooth radial primitive of [[lem-emg-local-potential-construction]] as the supplied $A_D$ with $dA_D=F^{(\epsilon)}|_D$. Adopt fixed-endpoint action stationarity only on sufficiently short finite curve segments contained in such a ball, as in [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]] and [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. There is no assumption that the whole trajectory lies in a single potential domain, that $F^{(\epsilon)}$ is globally exact, or that the local potentials are stationary. No inhomogeneous Maxwell or Einstein equation is imposed on this prescribed background. The dimensionless comparison trajectory satisfies $\mathbf X_N'=\mathbf W_N$, $\mathbf W_N'=-\nabla_X\phi(\mathbf X_N)+\mathbf e(\mathbf X_N)+\mathbf W_N\times\mathbf b(\mathbf X_N)$ on $[0,S_*]$, where primes denote $S$ derivatives, $S_*>0$, and $S=\sqrt\epsilon ct/L$. Write $\| (\mathbf X,\mathbf W)\|_1$ for the sum of the absolute values of the six components and $\|Df\|_{1\to1}$ for its induced operator norm, as in [[thm-emg-weak-slow-test-lorentz-limit]]. Let the six-component comparison vector field $f$ have derivative norm at most $L_f<\infty$ on a compact convex state set $\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathcal K\times\mathbb R^3$ containing both scaled trajectories throughout $[0,S_*]$.

Suppose a $C^2$ future-directed proper-time worldline exists through this finite interval, obeys this local action model (equivalently the external Lorentz law on each such segment), has coordinate speed $|\mathbf w|\le C_v\sqrt\epsilon c$, has its scaled state remain in $\mathcal Q$, and has the same initial scaled data as the comparison trajectory. Set $\mathbf X_\epsilon=\mathbf x/L$ and $\mathbf W_\epsilon=\mathbf w/(\sqrt\epsilon c)$. Then for some finite $C_r$ depending only on the displayed uniform bounds, the exact scaled motion obeys

$$\mathbf X_\epsilon'=\mathbf W_\epsilon,\qquad \mathbf W_\epsilon'=-\nabla_X\phi(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf e(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf W_\epsilon\times\mathbf b(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf r_\epsilon(S),\qquad \|\mathbf r_\epsilon(S)\|_1\le C_r\epsilon,$$

and consequently

$$\sup_{0\le S\le S_*}\bigl(\|\mathbf X_\epsilon-\mathbf X_N\|_1+\|\mathbf W_\epsilon-\mathbf W_N\|_1\bigr)\le C_r\epsilon S_*e^{L_fS_*}.$$

This is a finite-duration conditional model prediction. It does not construct the trajectories, prove common compact containment, solve Maxwell's equations for the prescribed field, or establish a coupled Einstein–Maxwell family. The magnetic scaling may violate a coupled stress hierarchy unless additional matter scales are supplied.

items.title: Electrostatic test-energy first integral
items.physical_scope: A finite-segment charged test probe in a prescribed, stationary electrostatic potential on Minkowski spacetime. The conserved energy is conditional on the adopted Lorentz-force law and excludes self-field, self-gravity, radiation reaction, and any coupled source claim.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2

items.statement:
On Minkowski spacetime with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, time orientation $\partial_0$, and length coordinates $x^0=ct$, let $\phi(\mathbf x)$ be a $C^2$ time-independent scalar potential on an open spatial region and set $A=-\phi(\mathbf x)\,dx^0/c$. Use SI units $[\phi]=\mathrm V$, $[q]=\mathrm C$, $[m]=\mathrm{kg}$, and $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ future-timelike proper-time segment satisfying the charged-probe law of [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]], define $\mathbf w=d\mathbf x/dt$ and $\gamma=(1-|\mathbf w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Then

$$E_{\mathrm{test}}=\gamma mc^2+q\phi(\mathbf x)$$

is constant along the segment. The field and metric are prescribed data; this is neither a measurement nor a coupled point-source solution.

items.title: Exact finite-frequency transverse Maxwell wave
items.physical_scope: An exact real, source-free plane-wave solution of the prescribed Minkowski Maxwell test model at every stated positive epsilon, with transverse electric/magnetic components. Its nonzero stress prevents it from solving the source-free coupled Einstein–Maxwell equation with Lambda=0 on the unchanged Minkowski metric. This is an ideal solution, not an experiment or photon-energy claim.

items.statement:
On Minkowski spacetime in standard positively oriented inertial coordinates $(x^0,x,y,z)$, with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and future unit observer $n=\partial_0$, choose constants $\kappa>0$ with units $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, $A_*\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ with units $\mathrm{T\,m}$, and dimensionless $0<\epsilon\le1$. Define

$$A_\epsilon=\epsilon A_*\cos\!\left(\frac{\kappa(x^0-z)}{\epsilon}\right)dx.$$

The real field $F_\epsilon=dA_\epsilon$ is an exact source-free Maxwell wave for every such $\epsilon$. Its nonzero components are

$$F_{0x}=-\kappa A_*\sin\!\left(\frac{\kappa(x^0-z)}{\epsilon}\right),\qquad F_{zx}=\kappa A_*\sin\!\left(\frac{\kappa(x^0-z)}{\epsilon}\right).$$

For the inertial observer $n=\partial_0$, the SI convention gives $E_x=c\kappa A_*\sin(\kappa(x^0-z)/\epsilon)$ and $B_y=\kappa A_*\sin(\kappa(x^0-z)/\epsilon)$, with all other components zero. At points where the sine is nonzero, the field energy is positive. The field is an exact test-background wave, but it is not an exact source-free coupled Einstein–Maxwell field with $\Lambda=0$ on the unchanged Minkowski metric.

items.title: Constant-magnetic-field slow test-orbit comparison
items.physical_scope: An exact finite-time comparison of a relativistic charged test orbit and its Newton–Lorentz slow-motion trajectory in a prescribed constant magnetic field on Minkowski space. It excludes self-field, radiation reaction, and any small-field backreaction theorem or fully coupled flat Einstein–Maxwell solution.

items.statement:
On Minkowski spacetime with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and time orientation $\partial_0$, set $\phi=0$, $\mathbf E=0$, and prescribe a constant magnetic field with $\alpha\mathbf B=\sqrt\epsilon(c/L)b_0\mathbf e_z$, where $\alpha=q/m\ne0$ has units $\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $b_0\ne0$ is dimensionless, $L>0$ has units metres, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$ is dimensionless. Choose initial velocity $\mathbf w_0=\sqrt\epsilon c\mathbf W_0$ with $\mathbf W_0\cdot\mathbf e_z=0$ and $\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|^2\le1/2$. Let $\mathbf X=\mathbf x/L$, $\mathbf W=\mathbf w/(\sqrt\epsilon c)$, and $S=\sqrt\epsilon ct/L$. With matched initial position, the exact relativistic and Newton–Lorentz comparison trajectories satisfy

$$|\mathbf W(S)-\mathbf W_N(S)|\le |b_0|\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|^3S,\qquad |\mathbf X(S)-\mathbf X_N(S)|\le\frac12|b_0|\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|^3S^2$$

on every fixed finite interval $0\le S\le S_*$. This is an exact ideal test-background comparison; it is not a coupled flat Einstein–Maxwell solution or a backreaction estimate.
